name: Waldorf Astoria Dubai International Financial Centre
positioning: High-rise Waldorf Astoria in Dubai's International Financial Centre, with an 18th-floor lobby, residential-style rooms inspired by a 1960s Manhattan apartment, and a rooftop pool lounge
best_for: Business travelers who want a DIFC base within 10 minutes of the Burj Khalifa and Dubai Mall
Couples who want a city stay with spa suites and a rooftop pool lounge

facts.text: The hotel is within 10 minutes of the Burj Khalifa, Dubai Mall and the Museum of the Future.
The lobby is on the 18th floor.
Rooms and suites are residential in style, with brass and walnut finishes, marble bathrooms stocked with Aesop products, and floor-to-ceiling windows with 180-degree views of the Dubai skyline.
Rooms are designed as a take on an upscale 1960s Manhattan apartment.
Interiors were largely designed by the American firm Smallwood, Reynolds, Stewart, Stewart and Associates.
Bull & Bear, the signature steakhouse, has an Art Deco setting on Level 18 with Burj Khalifa views.
Bull & Bear is modeled on the New York original, with dishes such as slow-cooked beef cheek, apple pie and a Waldorf salad.
Peacock Alley is a lounge and bar serving afternoon tea with sweet and savory bites.
The fitness centre has Technogym cardio and strength-training equipment.
Guests can choose a pillow from a Pillow Menu, and the Personal Concierge escorts guests to their room on arrival.
The property displays works by Lebanese artist Imad Bechara.
The ground-floor conference rooms include a show kitchen for interactive sessions.

highlights.text: The spa's floatation pod offers a sensory deprivation experience with 600 kg of Epsom salt.
St. Trop is a French Riviera-inspired rooftop lounge with a timber deck, pool, whirlpool and skyline views.
The Cigar Lounge evokes the 1960s Mad Men era and is hosted by a Cigar Sommelier.
Corner suites have two walls of floor-to-ceiling windows.
Every stay includes a dedicated Personal Concierge to help with excursions and special requests.

considerations.text: The hotel is across the street from DIFC's main thoroughfare, slightly away from the heaviest bar-hopping footfall.
Room amenities should be ordered through the Personal Concierge at least 48 hours before arrival.
WhataHotel notes the business district location may feel less resort-like.
